title: Components and parameters
summary: Build components, pass data down with parameters, and pass markup with RenderFragment.

predict.title: No [Parameter]
options: An error: `Greeting` has no parameter matching `Name`
predict.explanation: `Name` is public, but it has no **`[Parameter]`** attribute, so the parent can't set it. Blazor throws at runtime: *Object of type 'Greeting' does not have a property matching the name 'Name'*. Being public is not enough; the attribute is what makes it a parameter.

predict.title: The toggle that resets
options: An error, because a parameter was changed
predict.explanation: **Light 1: Off.** Clicking **+1** re-renders the page. `Label` changed, so Blazor passes the toggle's parameters again, **all of them**, including `IsOn="false"`. That overwrites the change the toggle made to its own parameter. A component should keep its own state in a **private field**, not in a `[Parameter]` property.

predict.title: Wrong name for the content
options: The card is empty, and **Hello** shows after it
The card is empty, with no error
predict.explanation:
Content written between a component's tags goes to a parameter named **`ChildContent`**. The name is a convention Blazor relies on. `Card` only has `Content`, so there is nowhere to put it, and Blazor reports that `Card` has no property matching `ChildContent`. Rename the parameter to `ChildContent`, or set it as `

Hello

`.

predict.title: A template
options: A build error: `context` is not defined
predict.explanation: `TItem` is inferred as `string` from `Items`. For each item, `ItemList` calls `ItemTemplate(item)`, and inside the template that item is called **`context`**. So you get one `<li>` per name: **ANA** and **BO**.

practice.title: Make it a real parameter
practice.task:
The page uses `<Alert Message="Saved" />` and crashes. Fix `Alert.razor`:

1. Make **`Message`** a parameter, and make the compiler warn when a parent forgets it.
2. Make **`Level`** a parameter with the default value `"info"`.

checks.hint: Write `[Parameter, EditorRequired] public string Message { get; set; } = "";`.

practice.title: Fix the toggle that resets
practice.task:
This toggle changes its own parameter, so it resets whenever the parent re-renders. Fix it:

1. Rename the parameter to **`InitialOn`**.
2. Keep the current state in a **private `bool` field** called **`isOn`**.
3. Copy `InitialOn` into `isOn` in **`OnInitialized`**.
4. The button changes `isOn`, never the parameter.

checks.label: A `[Parameter] public bool InitialOn` property
checks.hint: Rename the parameter: `[Parameter] public bool InitialOn { get; set; }`.

checks.label: A `private bool isOn;` field
checks.hint: Add `private bool isOn;` inside `@code`.

checks.label: `OnInitialized` copies `InitialOn` into `isOn`
checks.hint: Add `protected override void OnInitialized() { isOn = InitialOn; }`.

checks.label: Clicking flips `isOn` (`isOn = !isOn`)
checks.hint: Use `@onclick="() => isOn = !isOn"`.

checks.label: Nothing writes to the parameter `InitialOn` except a default
checks.hint: Only read `InitialOn`. Change `isOn` instead.

checks.label: The old `IsOn` parameter is gone
checks.hint: Replace every `IsOn` with `isOn` (the field) or `InitialOn` (the parameter).

practice.title: A generic list, from scratch
practice.task:
Write **`ItemList.razor`**, a generic component:

- A type parameter **`TItem`**.
- A parameter **`Items`** of type `IEnumerable<TItem>`.
- A parameter **`ItemTemplate`** of type `RenderFragment<TItem>`.
- It renders a `<ul>` with one `<li>` per item, using the template.

It will be used like this:

```razor
<ItemList Items="products">
    <ItemTemplate>@context.Name</ItemTemplate>
</ItemList>
```

checks.label: `@typeparam TItem`
checks.hint: Start with `@typeparam TItem`.

checks.label: A parameter `IEnumerable<TItem> Items`
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public IEnumerable<TItem> Items { get; set; } = [];`.

checks.label: A parameter `RenderFragment<TItem> ItemTemplate`
checks.hint: Add `[Parameter] public RenderFragment<TItem> ItemTemplate { get; set; } = default!;`.

checks.label: Loops over `Items` with `@foreach`
checks.hint: Use `@foreach (var item in Items) { ... }` inside the `<ul>`.

checks.hint:

quiz.body: An AI tool created `Components/Shared/UserCard.razor`. What is the C# class it compiles to?
options: `UserCard`, in a namespace based on the folder (like `MyApp.Components.Shared`)
There is no class: `.razor` files are templates, not C#
quiz.explanation: A `.razor` file compiles to a (partial) **class with the same name as the file**. The namespace comes from the project and folder, unless `@namespace` changes it.

quiz.body: What does `[EditorRequired]` do on a parameter?
options: The app throws if the parent doesn't set it
The compiler shows a **warning** if a parent doesn't set it
It hides the parameter from IntelliSense
quiz.explanation: `[EditorRequired]` is a **build-time warning** (`RZ2012`) for a missing parameter. At runtime nothing checks it, so still give it a safe default or check for `null`.

quiz.body: A parent passes `Title="@title"` to a child. Later `title` changes and the parent re-renders. What happens to the child's `Title`?
options: Nothing: parameters are only set once, when the child is created
The parent sets the child's parameters again, so `Title` gets the parent's current value
The child must call `StateHasChanged()` to get the new value
The child is destroyed and created again
quiz.explanation: Each time the parent renders, Blazor passes the parameters again (`SetParametersAsync`). The child keeps its instance, but its parameters are **overwritten** with the parent's values. This is why a child should not change its own parameters.

quiz.body: You use `<PriceTag Value="9.99" />` in a page, but on screen nothing appears and the HTML contains a `<pricetag>` element. What is the most likely cause?
options: The `PriceTag` namespace is not imported (`@using` is missing), so it is treated as a plain HTML element
quiz.explanation: If the compiler can't find a component with that name, it renders the tag as an HTML element and shows only a **warning** (`RZ10012`). Add `@using` for its namespace, in the file or in `_Imports.razor`.

quiz.body: `Panel` has two `RenderFragment` parameters: `Header` and `Body`. Which usage is correct?
quiz.explanation: Set each `RenderFragment` with a **child element named after the parameter**. A string attribute is not markup, and loose content would go to `ChildContent`, which `Panel` doesn't have.

options: The current `Product` passed to the template
quiz.explanation: For a `RenderFragment<T>`, `context` is the **value of type `T`** the component passes when it calls the template. Rename it with `Context="product"` on the template element.

quiz.body: What does `[Parameter(CaptureUnmatchedValues = true)] public Dictionary<string, object>? Extra { get; set; }` do?
options: It collects every attribute the parent sets that doesn't match another parameter
It stores the values of all other parameters, for debugging
It lets the parent set any C# property of the component
It caches parameter values between renders
quiz.explanation: Attributes that don't match a parameter (like `class`, `placeholder`, `aria-label`) go into this dictionary. Then `@attributes="Extra"` puts them on an element. This is **attribute splatting**.

quiz.body: A component renders `<input class="base" @attributes="Extra" />`. The parent passes `class="big"`, which is captured in `Extra`. What is the input's class?
quiz.explanation: Attributes are applied **left to right, and the last one wins**. `@attributes` comes after `class="base"`, so the captured `class="big"` wins. To make the component's value win, write `class` **after** `@attributes`.

quiz.body: You move a component's `@code` into `Alert.razor.cs`. What must the C# file contain?
options: `public class Alert : ComponentBase` in any namespace
`public partial class Alert`, in the **same namespace** as `Alert.razor`
`public class AlertCode`, and `@inherits AlertCode` in the `.razor` file is optional
quiz.explanation: The `.razor` file compiles to a **partial class**, so the code-behind is the other half: `partial`, same class name, same namespace. (`@inherits` with a base class is another, older pattern.)

quiz.body: `Greeting` has `[Parameter] public string Name { get; set; }`. The page writes `<Greeting Name="user.Name" />`. What does it show?
quiz.explanation: For a **string** parameter, the attribute value is plain text, so you get the literal text `user.Name`. Write `Name="@user.Name"` to pass the C# value. (For non-string parameters like `int`, the value is already treated as C#.)

interview.question: What is a Razor component?
interview.modelAnswer: A reusable piece of UI in a `.razor` file: markup plus C# in an `@code` block. It compiles to a C# class named after the file. You use it like an HTML tag, and with `@page` it also becomes a routable page.

interview.question: How does a parent pass data to a child component?
interview.modelAnswer: Through parameters: public properties marked `[Parameter]`, set as attributes on the child's tag. Data flows one way, parent to child, and is passed again every time the parent re-renders.

interview.question: What does `[EditorRequired]` do?
interview.modelAnswer: It makes the compiler warn when a parent doesn't set that parameter. It's only a build-time warning: nothing enforces it at runtime, so the component should still handle a missing value.

interview.question: Why shouldn't a component change its own `[Parameter]` properties?
interview.modelAnswer: Because the parent overwrites them the next time it re-renders, so the change is lost and the UI 'resets'. Keep internal state in a private field (initialized from the parameter), or ask the parent to change the value through an `EventCallback`.

interview.question: What is `RenderFragment`, and what is `ChildContent`?
interview.modelAnswer: A `RenderFragment` is a piece of UI passed as a value, so a component can render markup supplied by its parent. A `RenderFragment` parameter named `ChildContent` receives whatever the parent writes between the component's opening and closing tags.

interview.question: What is a templated component?
interview.modelAnswer: A component that takes `RenderFragment<T>` parameters, so the parent decides how each item is rendered. It is often generic with `@typeparam`. Inside the template, the item is available as `context`. Grids and lists are typical examples.

interview.question: What is attribute splatting?
interview.modelAnswer: Capturing attributes that don't match any parameter with `[Parameter(CaptureUnmatchedValues = true)]` into a dictionary, then applying them to an element with `@attributes`. It lets a wrapper component accept `class`, `id`, `aria-*` and so on. The last attribute written wins.

interview.question: How do you split a component's markup and C# into two files?
interview.modelAnswer: Put the C# in `Name.razor.cs` as `public partial class Name` in the same namespace. The `.razor` file compiles to the other half of the partial class. Services are injected with `[Inject]` properties instead of `@inject`.
